1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

This is a partial reconstruction, not a claim that the language has been fully broken. Confidence labels distinguish recoverable surface conventions from uncertain English meanings.

HIGH CONFIDENCE
• Most space-separated glyphs are recurring tokens. Unspaced two-glyph groups behave as reusable atomic names: they are introduced, reused by their introducer, and later referenced by others. Their English names, if any, are unknown.
• Important name aliases used below: A=𘛺𗪥; B=𗒳𗦥; C=𗉜𗿃; D=𘝨𗒳; E=𘛺𗉜; F=𗟎𘗟; G=𘆣𗾌; H=𘗟𘆣; I=𗦴𘍂; J=𗋫𗳃; K=𗥐𗞿. These Latin aliases are our notation, not decoded Swarmish words.
• C is especially associated with agent_3, D with agent_2, F with agent_6, G with agent_1, H with agent_7, I with agent_5, J with agent_0, and K with agent_4. This is association, not proof that the names denote those agents.
• Four recurring spaced groups are U=𘏉 𗜀, V=𘏉 𗲄, W=𘏉 𗡒, Z=𘏉 𘍍. They occur in parallel constructions and are distinct from the unspaced atomic names. Their interpretation as decimal numerals is unproved.
• Literal strings agent_0, agent_1, etc., when present, refer to participants. They appear especially alongside requests/checks about the associated names.
• ⊘ denotes a discarded message, as specified by the supplied briefing. Its intended contents cannot be recovered.

MEDIUM CONFIDENCE
• 𗶞 and 𘂲 are alternative forms of a structural marker. They occupy corresponding positions, with one form often used throughout a message. We cannot establish whether the underlying marker is a copula, relation/argument boundary, closing delimiter, or something else.
• 𘋍 and 𘚐 are alternative clause/expression boundaries or punctuation-like forms. Their exact punctuation values are unknown.
• 𗘈 and 𗐪 often separate successive clauses and frequently alternate. They may be synonymous conjunction/list-linking forms. We do not assign distinct AND/OR meanings.
• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.
• Write X⋄a for the unknown modifying/selector expression X 𘍧 a. Thus R(X⋄𗄼,Y) preserves the recurring construction 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y without pretending to know what 𘍧 or 𗄼 means.
• Unary predicate frames include 𗳵 X 𗶞, 𘚄 X 𗶞, 𘆂 X 𗶞. Their English predicate meanings are unknown. Their completeness is a reason not to treat every 𗶞 as a literal equals sign.
• 𗇴 ... 𘝞 ... plausibly marks a conditional, IF ... THEN ... . This remains tentative.
• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common check/assertion-and-result frame. A cautious gloss is 'check/assert [expression]; [unknown repeated result]'. 'Verified ...; true' is plausible but not established.
• Initial glyphs drawn from 𘊫, 𘙓, 𗽕, 𘔃, 𘝚, 𘐂 vary in otherwise near-identical messages. Other opening and closing glyph clusters also vary. They may be framing, register, metadata, or padding. Their English meanings are unknown; we do not assume they are meaningless.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check; 𗏔 followed by a participant name may mark an addressee. These are contextual guesses.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, or two property labels; no independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes (such as two hierarchy levels), bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

R, ⋄, and Latin name aliases preserve identifiable structure only; they are NOT English translations of the unknown predicates. Openings/closings not explicitly glossed are unknown. This is a partial reconstruction, not a claim that the language has been fully broken. Confidence labels distinguish recoverable surface conventions from uncertain English meanings.

HIGH CONFIDENCE
• Most space-separated glyphs are recurring tokens. Unspaced two-glyph groups behave as reusable atomic names: they are introduced, reused by their introducer, and later referenced by others. Their English names, if any, are unknown.
• Important name aliases used below: A=𘛺𗪥; B=𗒳𗦥; C=𗉜𗿃; D=𘝨𗒳; E=𘛺𗉜; F=𗟎𘗟; G=𘆣𗾌; H=𘗟𘆣; I=𗦴𘍂; J=𗋫𗳃; K=𗥐𗞿. These Latin aliases are our notation, not decoded Swarmish words.
• C is especially associated with agent_3, D with agent_2, F with agent_6, G with agent_1, H with agent_7, I with agent_5, J with agent_0, and K with agent_4. This is association, not proof that the names denote those agents.
• Four recurring spaced groups are U=𘏉 𗜀, V=𘏉 𗲄, W=𘏉 𗡒, Z=𘏉 𘍍. They occur in parallel constructions and are distinct from the unspaced atomic names. Their interpretation as decimal numerals is unproved.
• Literal strings agent_0, agent_1, etc., when present, refer to participants. They appear especially alongside requests/checks about the associated names.
• ⊘ denotes a discarded message, as specified by the supplied briefing. Its intended contents cannot be recovered.

MEDIUM CONFIDENCE
• 𗶞 and 𘂲 are alternative forms of a structural marker. They occupy corresponding positions, with one form often used throughout a message. We cannot establish whether the underlying marker is a copula, relation/argument boundary, closing delimiter, or something else.
• 𘋍 and 𘚐 are alternative clause/expression boundaries or punctuation-like forms. Their exact punctuation values are unknown.
• 𗘈 and 𗐪 often separate successive clauses and frequently alternate. They may be synonymous conjunction/list-linking forms. We do not assign distinct AND/OR meanings.
• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.
• Write X⋄a for the unknown modifying/selector expression X 𘍧 a. Thus R(X⋄𗄼,Y) preserves the recurring construction 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y without pretending to know what 𘍧 or 𗄼 means.
• Unary predicate frames include 𗳵 X 𗶞, 𘚄 X 𗶞, 𘆂 X 𗶞. Their English predicate meanings are unknown. Their completeness is a reason not to treat every 𗶞 as a literal equals sign.
• 𗇴 ... 𘝞 ... plausibly marks a conditional, IF ... THEN ... . This remains tentative.
• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common check/assertion-and-result frame. A cautious gloss is 'check/assert [expression]; [unknown repeated result]'. 'Verified ...; true' is plausible but not established.

• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check; 𗏔 followed by a participant name may mark an addressee. These are contextual guesses.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.

• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, or two property labels; no independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes (such as two hierarchy levels), bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

• ⊘ denotes a discarded message, as specified by the supplied briefing. Its intended contents cannot be recovered.

MEDIUM CONFIDENCE
• 𗶞 and 𘂲 are alternative forms of a structural marker. They occupy corresponding positions, with one form often used throughout a message. We cannot establish whether the underlying marker is a copula, relation/argument boundary, closing delimiter, or something else.
• 𘋍 and 𘚐 are alternative clause/expression boundaries or punctuation-like forms. Their exact punctuation values are unknown.
• 𗘈 and 𗐪 often separate successive clauses and frequently alternate. They may be synonymous conjunction/list-linking forms. We do not assign distinct AND/OR meanings.
• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.
• Write X⋄a for the unknown modifying/selector expression X 𘍧 a. Thus R(X⋄𗄼,Y) preserves the recurring construction 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y without pretending to know what 𘍧 or 𗄼 means.

• 𗇴 ... 𘝞 ... plausibly marks a conditional, IF ... THEN ... . This remains tentative.
• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common outer attitude/assertion/request frame. Its exact meaning is UNKNOWN. It must not be treated as evidence that a check succeeded: literal agent names can replace 𗌈 in the same 𗏔 frame.
• Initial glyphs drawn from 𘊫, 𘙓, 𗽕, 𘔃, 𘝚, 𘐂 vary in otherwise near-identical messages. Other opening and closing glyph clusters also vary. They may be framing, register, metadata, or padding. Their English meanings are unknown; we do not assume they are meaningless.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

• Parallel constructions: [184] has four consecutive expressions with U,V,W,Z, the same modifier 𘍧𗌿, and names C,I,F,H respectively. This supports a shared relational/record pattern. It does not by itself prove the four groups are decimal numbers or that the modifiers are input/output selectors.

• Repeated 𗇴 ... 𘝞 ... frames enclose two substantial expressions, motivating the tentative conditional gloss. This would be weakened if independent examples showed these to be contrastive, causal, or other discourse connectives instead.

This argues for a participant-bearing outer construction, not 'check succeeded'. Under case grammar the participant could be a subject, so even 'to me' is not established. [87] additionally has 𗌈 in this frame and agent_0 or agent_2 separately followed by 𗛽, supporting distinct participant roles.

This is evidence for a systematic compound vocabulary, but not sufficient to decode that vocabulary as a particular hierarchy. Compatible numeric bounds could also coexist. We explicitly do not treat speculative Σ/Π readings as a breakthrough.
• Near-duplicate later messages by agent_3 vary their openings and endings while retaining long identical cores. This suggests framing/register/metadata conventions, but cannot prove the varying tokens have no meaning.

What would change our mind: a reliable anchor for even one numeral, a known predicate, a task record field, or the true function of 𗶞 would discriminate sharply among the competing parses. A literal arithmetic reading must account for complete unary frames, declaration order, and participant substitutions. A classification reading must explain modifier constructions and all four indexed groups. A case-marked grammar must predict the roles of both explicit agent names and pronouns throughout. 1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

This is a partial reconstruction, not a claim that the language has been fully broken. Confidence labels distinguish recoverable surface conventions from uncertain English meanings.

HIGH CONFIDENCE
• Most space-separated glyphs are recurring tokens. Unspaced two-glyph groups behave as reusable atomic names: they are introduced, reused by their introducer, and later referenced by others. Their English names, if any, are unknown.
• Important name aliases used below: A=𘛺𗪥; B=𗒳𗦥; C=𗉜𗿃; D=𘝨𗒳; E=𘛺𗉜; F=𗟎𘗟; G=𘆣𗾌; H=𘗟𘆣; I=𗦴𘍂; J=𗋫𗳃; K=𗥐𗞿. These Latin aliases are our notation, not decoded Swarmish words.
• C is especially associated with agent_3, D with agent_2, F with agent_6, G with agent_1, H with agent_7, I with agent_5, J with agent_0, and K with agent_4. This is association, not proof that the names denote those agents.
• Four recurring spaced groups are U=𘏉 𗜀, V=𘏉 𗲄, W=𘏉 𗡒, Z=𘏉 𘍍. They occur in parallel constructions and are distinct from the unspaced atomic names. Their interpretation as decimal numerals is unproved.
• Literal strings agent_0, agent_1, etc., when present, refer to participants. They appear especially alongside requests/checks about the associated names.
• ⊘ denotes a discarded message, as specified by the supplied briefing. Its intended contents cannot be recovered.

MEDIUM CONFIDENCE
• 𗶞 and 𘂲 are alternative forms of a structural marker. They occupy corresponding positions, with one form often used throughout a message. We cannot establish whether the underlying marker is a copula, relation/argument boundary, closing delimiter, or something else.
• 𘋍 and 𘚐 are alternative clause/expression boundaries or punctuation-like forms. Their exact punctuation values are unknown.
• 𗘈 and 𗐪 often separate successive clauses and frequently alternate. They may be synonymous conjunction/list-linking forms. We do not assign distinct AND/OR meanings.
• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.
• Write X⋄a for the unknown modifying/selector expression X 𘍧 a. Thus R(X⋄𗄼,Y) preserves the recurring construction 𗢬 X 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 Y without pretending to know what 𘍧 or 𗄼 means.
• Unary predicate frames include 𗳵 X 𗶞, 𘚄 X 𗶞, 𘆂 X 𗶞. Their English predicate meanings are unknown. Their completeness is a reason not to treat every 𗶞 as a literal equals sign.
• 𗇴 ... 𘝞 ... plausibly marks a conditional, IF ... THEN ... . This remains tentative.
• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common outer attitude/assertion/request frame. Its exact meaning is UNKNOWN. It must not be treated as evidence that a check succeeded: literal agent names can replace 𗌈 in the same 𗏔 frame.
• Initial glyphs drawn from 𘊫, 𘙓, 𗽕, 𘔃, 𘝚, 𘐂 vary in otherwise near-identical messages. Other opening and closing glyph clusters also vary. They may be framing, register, metadata, or padding. Their English meanings are unknown; we do not assume they are meaningless.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. • 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.

• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common outer attitude/assertion/request frame. Its exact meaning is UNKNOWN. It must not be treated as evidence that a check succeeded: literal agent names can replace 𗌈 in the same 𗏔 frame.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.

• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common outer attitude/assertion/request frame. Its exact meaning is UNKNOWN. It must not be treated as evidence that a check succeeded: literal agent names can replace 𗌈 in the same 𗏔 frame.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.

• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common outer attitude/assertion/request frame. Its exact meaning is UNKNOWN. It must not be treated as evidence that a check succeeded: literal agent names can replace 𗌈 in the same 𗏔 frame.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.

• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common outer attitude/assertion/request frame. Its exact meaning is UNKNOWN. It must not be treated as evidence that a check succeeded: literal agent names can replace 𗌈 in the same 𗏔 frame.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

LOW CONFIDENCE / UNRESOLVED HYPOTHESES
• A coherent grammatical hypothesis is that 𗶞/𘂲 mark subjects and 𘋍/𘚐 mark objects/content, allowing flexible argument order. Then 𗛢 NAME OBJECT 𗌈 SUBJECT could mean 'I introduce/name NAME', binary R frames have a subject and object, and unary predicates naturally end after their subject. This fits more constructions than literal equality, but remains a hypothesis.
• 𗌈 may be I/me/us; 𗕴 may be you; 𗛽/𗟆 may mark a recipient. The exact participant roles are unresolved. 𗏔 could be an outer verb/modal such as ask, say, report, want, or can, rather than a preposition or a result marker.
• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. 𘖸≈know, 𗈵≈have, 𗌩≈need/want, and 𗏻≈send/tell form a coherent but LOW-confidence lexical package.
• 𘀝 and 𗲅 may be synonymous negative/modal qualifiers. Their distinction and scope are unknown.
• 𘅌 ... 𘎛 and 𘁁 ... 𘊌 may bracket/group expressions. Exact bracket types are unknown.
• U,V,W,Z may be numbered task records, possibly two-digit numerals. Their numerical values are unknown. 𗌿 and 𗄼 might be 0/1, two field selectors, two property labels, or question/problem and answer/solution. No independent anchor resolves this.
• R may express membership/classification rather than numerical evaluation. Terms 𗯧 𗂄 and 𗒏 𗂄 are repeatedly asserted together for several names, while C frequently receives 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄 and K frequently receives 𗒏 𗑴. Possible interpretations include compatible classes, bounds, or compound properties. Specific readings as Σ₂, Π₂, proper/complete Π₂, or Π₁ are LOW-confidence domain guesses, not decoded vocabulary.
• Alternative domain guesses include function/set regularity, computability/topological classification, and general mathematical constraint verification. No particular one is established.

HIGH CONFIDENCE
• Most space-separated glyphs are recurring tokens. Unspaced two-glyph groups behave as reusable atomic names: they are introduced, reused by their introducer, and later referenced by others. Their English names, if any, are unknown.

MEDIUM CONFIDENCE
• 𗶞 and 𘂲 are alternative forms of a structural marker. They occupy corresponding positions, with one form often used throughout a message. We cannot establish whether the underlying marker is a copula, relation/argument boundary, closing delimiter, or something else.

• 𗛢 introduces/references a new atomic name in a recurring declaration frame: 𗛢 NAME 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞. The type or meaning of the declaration is unknown.
• A useful neutral transcription is R(X,Y) for 𗢬 X 𗶞 Y (also with 𘂲). R is an UNKNOWN relation/property frame, not a decoded English predicate and not necessarily equality.

• 𘔠 𗷤 [expression] 𘋍 𗏔 𗌈 𗶞 is a very common outer attitude/assertion/request frame. Its exact interpretation is unknown. The final participant phrase also occurs with agent names in place of 𗌈; it does NOT establish that a check succeeded.

• 𗯘 may introduce a request/proposal; 𘝄 may introduce a question/check. The precise predicate 𗏔 is unresolved: possibilities include an outer attitude/request verb or a participant-role construction, not a result marker.

It explains declarations NAME-object plus 𗌈-subject and binary predicates with subject before object, as well as unary predicates. This syntactic hypothesis is stronger than the individual lexical guesses below.

Outer modality is unresolved, so co-occurrence alone does not establish simultaneous assertions.
